description: Host acceptance scenarios (SPEC 6, 7, 8.3, 8.4, 9.1). Each scenario is one host's view of one repository: create a rules engine for `hostKey` (a.vault.example) with head bound `headBound`, apply `steps` in order, and each step's verdict MUST equal `expect` ("ok" or the SPEC 10.4 code). Then the accepted commits with no accepted child MUST be exactly `finalHeads`, the held commits (SPEC 6.5) exactly `finalHeld`, and the winning chain's tip manifestHash `finalTip` (null when no state was accepted). When a scenario has `finalLeaves`, the pending leave requests (SPEC 8.4, one per member) MUST be exactly those `{ memberKey, at }`. A stored commit whose removal cutoff cannot yet be decided (SPEC 7.3) is neither a head nor held. Steps: `op` is manifest, commit, or leave. A manifest step's `item` is `{ manifest: SignedManifest, commit?: Commit }`, the publishManifest body: the commit is the genesis commit (createRepo), the rotation commit of an epoch-raising state, or absent; the state and its commit are applied together or not at all (SPEC 8.2, 8.3). A commit step's `item` is a Commit; a leave step's `item` is a LeaveRequest. `via` is the path: "push" is a client write (push, createRepo, publishManifest, leave) whose authenticated caller is the commit author, the owner for a manifest, or memberKey for a leave, with the head bound applied; "offer" is replication from a peer host (SPEC 9.1): no caller check and no head bound. A held commit answers forbidden on either path. `label` names the item for reading only. Every expectation is written by hand from the SPEC rule each description cites. Keys, hosts, data keys, and wraps are those of manifest.json, plus an epoch 2 data key (32 bytes of 0x44) used only by content-epoch-jump-2; each commit's payload is {"v":2,"accounts":{}} under AAD v2 with IV SHA-256(UTF8("avp/vectors/acceptance-iv/" + label))[0..12]. Where two diverged states must hash in a set order, the losing one's wraps use the label "<member>/g<i>" for the first i that puts its manifestHash above the winner's. Generated by vectors/generate.ts.

scenarios.name: genesis-ok
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.2, 8.2: a valid genesis state that lists this host, published with a first commit that has no parents, cites seq 1 and the genesis hash, is by the owner at epoch 0: both are accepted and the commit is the only head.

scenarios.name: genesis-wrong-repo-id
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.2, 4.2: the genesis repoId does not recompute from ownerKey and genesisNonce (it was derived from another nonce), so the state is rejected (bad_request) and its commit with it.

scenarios.name: genesis-host-not-listed
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 rule 6, 8.2: a valid genesis whose hosts list only b.vault.example, applied at a.vault.example: not_hosted, nothing stored.

scenarios.name: manifest-seq-skip
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 rule 4, 6.3: a seq 3 state arrives while the tip is seq 1 (its seq 2 predecessor never arrived); its seq is not tip + 1, so manifest_conflict.

scenarios.name: manifest-bad-owner-sig
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 rule 2: a seq 2 state whose ownerSignature is alice's signature, not the owner's: bad_request; the tip stays at genesis.

scenarios.name: manifest-rollback
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.3, 6.4, 12.3: after seq 2 and seq 3 are accepted, the seq 2 state is published again; its seq is not tip + 1, so manifest_conflict, and the tip stays at seq 3.

scenarios.name: manifest-member-dropped-without-removal
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 rule 5: a seq 3 state drops bob from members without a removal: bad_request.

scenarios.name: manifest-removal-without-epoch-bump
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 rule 5: a seq 3 state adds a removal but keeps keyEpoch 0; a state that adds a removal MUST raise keyEpoch by one: bad_request.

scenarios.name: commit-non-member
scenarios.description: SPEC 7.1, 7.2: carol, who is not a member, commits under genesis: forbidden on push (the caller is not a member of the tip) and forbidden by replication (the author is not a member of the cited state).

scenarios.name: commit-epoch-mismatch
scenarios.description: SPEC 7.2: alice cites seq 2 (keyEpoch 0) but writes keyEpoch 1: forbidden.

scenarios.name: commit-unknown-parent
scenarios.description: SPEC 7.4: a1's parent a0 is unknown: missing_parents, which is retryable; once a0 is accepted the same a1 is accepted.

scenarios.name: commit-unknown-manifest
scenarios.description: SPEC 7.2 manifest binding: a commit citing a validly signed state this host never received gets missing_parents; so does one citing seq 3 with the seq 2 manifestHash, since the pair names no held state.

scenarios.name: commit-id-mismatch
scenarios.description: SPEC 7.1: a1 with one ciphertext byte flipped but its commitId and signature kept: the id does not recompute, bad_request; the untampered a1 is then accepted.

scenarios.name: commit-bad-author-signature
scenarios.description: SPEC 7.1: a1 whose authorSignature is bob's signature over a1's id: it does not verify under the author (alice), bad_request.

scenarios.name: commit-wrong-repo-id
scenarios.description: SPEC 7.1: a commit whose repoId is another repository's: bad_request.

scenarios.name: commit-repush-idempotent
scenarios.description: SPEC 7, 12.3: a commit the host already holds is accepted again with no change, by push and by replication.

scenarios.name: commit-citing-older-state-ok
scenarios.description: SPEC 7.2: after seq 3 adds bob, alice's commit citing seq 2 (where she is a member at epoch 0) is still valid.

scenarios.name: concurrent-commits-two-heads
scenarios.description: SPEC 7.4: alice and bob each write a child of the root; both are accepted and both are heads.

scenarios.name: merge-collapses-heads
scenarios.description: SPEC 7.4, 5: a merge commit naming both heads as parents is accepted and becomes the only head.

scenarios.name: merge-at-head-bound
scenarios.description: SPEC 7.4: sixteen children of the root give sixteen heads (the sixteenth push leaves exactly the bound, which is allowed); a merge of two of them would leave 16 - 2 + 1 = 15 heads and MUST be accepted at the bound.

scenarios.name: seventeenth-head-rejected
scenarios.description: SPEC 7.4: with sixteen heads, a client push of a seventeenth child of the root would leave 17 heads, more than the bound: too_many_heads.

scenarios.name: head-bound-exempt-for-replication
scenarios.description: SPEC 7.4, 9.1: the head bound applies to client pushes only. With sixteen heads, head-17 by replication is accepted (17 heads); a push of head-18 would leave 18: too_many_heads; a merge of two heads would leave 17 - 2 + 1 = 16 and is accepted.

scenarios.name: removed-member-frontier-ok
scenarios.description: SPEC 7.3, 8.3: seq 3 removes bob with frontier {a1, b1, b2}; the rotation commit merges a1 and b1. b2, bob's commit the owner saw but this host had not, then arrives by replication: its id is in the frontier, so it is accepted (citing seq 2 at epoch 0) and is a head beside the rotation commit.

scenarios.name: removed-member-after-cutoff
scenarios.description: SPEC 7.3, 7.4: after seq 3 removes bob with frontier {a1, b1}, bob's b3 (a child of the root, citing seq 2 at epoch 0) is neither in the frontier nor an ancestor of a frontier commit: forbidden by replication and on push. alice's child of b3 then has a rejected parent: forbidden.

scenarios.name: removed-member-backdated-child-of-frontier
scenarios.description: SPEC 7.3: after bob's removal with frontier {a1, b1}, bob backdates b4 citing seq 2 at epoch 0 with parent b1, which is in the frontier. b4's own id is neither in the frontier nor an ancestor of a frontier commit, so it MUST be rejected: forbidden by replication and on push.

scenarios.name: removed-member-ancestor-of-frontier
scenarios.description: SPEC 7.3: the frontier is {a1, b1, b2} and b2's parent is b0, both unseen here. b0 first: the host lacks frontier commit b2 and cannot decide, so missing_parents. b2: in the frontier but its parent b0 is unknown, missing_parents (its verified header now counts for ancestry). b0 again: an ancestor of frontier commit b2, accepted. b2 again: accepted.

scenarios.name: removed-member-dropped-on-removal
scenarios.description: SPEC 7.3: this host holds bob's head b1, which never reached the owner; seq 3 removes bob with frontier {a1}. On accepting it the host re-checks bob's commits and drops b1 from the heads; alice's later child of b1 has a rejected parent: forbidden.

scenarios.name: rotation-without-commit
scenarios.description: SPEC 8.3, 9.1: seq 3 removes bob and raises the epoch; without its rotation commit it is rejected with bad_request, by replication and on publish. Published with it, both are accepted.

scenarios.name: rotation-commit-not-owner
scenarios.description: SPEC 8.3: the rotation commit of an epoch-raising state MUST be authored by ownerKey; one by alice is bad_request and the state is not adopted either (atomic).

scenarios.name: rotation-commit-wrong-epoch
scenarios.description: SPEC 8.3: the rotation commit MUST be at the new epoch (1); one at epoch 0 is bad_request and the state is not adopted.

scenarios.name: rotation-commit-missing-parent
scenarios.description: SPEC 8.3 atomicity, 7.2, 7.4: the rotation commit's parent x is unknown, so the pair answers missing_parents and neither is stored: alice's commit citing seq 3 then gets missing_parents too (unknown state). Once x is accepted, the pair and then alice's commit are accepted.

scenarios.name: diverged-owner-lower-hash-wins
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.5 tie rule: two owner-signed seq 2 states, X2 (adds alice) with the bytewise-lower manifestHash and Y2 (adds carol). The host holds Y2, then receives X2 and switches to it; Y2 offered again loses (manifest_conflict). alice is a member; carol, invited only on the losing chain, is not, so her push is forbidden.

scenarios.name: diverged-owner-higher-hash-loses
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.5, 7.2: holding X2 (lower hash), the host is offered Y2: it loses the tie rule, manifest_conflict, and is retained as a verified losing state. carol's commit citing Y2 then resolves (not missing_parents) and is re-checked: X2 does not list carol and the tip epoch has not passed hers, so it is held (forbidden).

scenarios.name: diverged-owner-commit-rechecked-ok
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.5: the host holds H3 (adds bob) and accepts alice's a1 citing it; then L3 (adds carol, lower hash) wins. a1 now cites a losing state and is re-checked against L3, which lists alice at the same epoch 0: it stays accepted. A new a2 citing H3 is accepted the same way.

scenarios.name: diverged-owner-commit-held
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.5: one owner device removes bob (L3, epoch 1, with rotation commit rotL), the other adds carol (W3, epoch 0, lower hash). The host accepts L3, rotL, and alice's a1 at epoch 1; then W3 wins. rotL and a1 cite a losing state, W3 does not list them at epoch 1, and the tip epoch (0) has not passed theirs: they are held (rotL kept with its state, SPEC 8.3) and leave the heads. A push of a1, or of a new a2 citing L3, answers forbidden.

scenarios.name: held-commit-accepted-after-reinvite
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.5: carol is invited only on the losing L3; her c1 citing L3 is accepted while L3 is the tip, then held when W3 (policy flip, lower hash) wins; her push is forbidden while she is not a member. W4 re-invites carol at the same epoch 0: the held c1 is re-checked against W4 and accepted.

scenarios.name: held-commit-dropped-after-epoch
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.5: carol's c1 and its child c2 cite the losing L3; when W3 (lower hash) wins they are held. W4 removes bob and raises the epoch to 1: re-checked against W4, c1 meets the drop test (tip epoch 1 exceeds its 0) and is dropped permanently, c2 with it. Offering c1 again is forbidden, and a new c3 citing L3 meets the drop test at its first classification: forbidden.

scenarios.name: leave-bad-signature
scenarios.description: SPEC 8.4: a leave request for alice whose signature is bob's: it does not verify under memberKey, bad_request.

scenarios.name: leave-ok
scenarios.description: SPEC 8.4: alice, a member of the tip and not the owner, publishes a validly signed leave request: accepted.

scenarios.name: leave-non-member
scenarios.description: SPEC 8.4: carol, not a member of the tip, publishes a validly signed leave request: forbidden.

scenarios.name: leave-owner
scenarios.description: SPEC 8.4: the owner cannot leave its own repository: forbidden.

scenarios.name: removed-member-undecided-then-dropped
scenarios.description: SPEC 7.3: bob's b3 is accepted while bob is a member. seq 3 removes bob with frontier {a1, b1, b2}; b2 is unknown, so the host cannot decide b3 and MUST NOT keep accepting it (it leaves the heads, undecided, not dropped). b0 and b2 arrive (each first missing_parents); once b2's verified header is known, the frontier's ancestry is complete, b3 is neither in it nor an ancestor of it, and b3 is dropped. b0 and b2 are then accepted.

scenarios.name: removed-member-undecided-held-kept
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.5, 7.3: holding W3, the host is offered the losing L3 (epoch 1) with its rotation commit rotL, which is kept held (SPEC 8.3); alice's a2 citing L3 at epoch 1 is held. W4 removes alice (epoch 1) with frontier {x}, a commit this host never saw. Deciding the held commits against W4: rotL meets no drop test and W4 lists the owner at epoch 1, so it is accepted; for a2 the cutoff cannot be decided without x, so a2 is neither accepted (W4 does not list alice) nor dropped: it stays held.

scenarios.name: diverged-owner-publish-needs-tip-plus-one
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.3, 6.5: holding Y2 (adds carol), the host gets a client publish of X2 (adds alice), whose manifestHash is lower. A host accepts a state from a client only at tip + 1 linked to the tip, so the publish is manifest_conflict and the tip stays Y2 (X2 is kept as a verified losing state). The same X2 by replication wins the tie rule and becomes the tip.

scenarios.name: genesis-without-commit
scenarios.description: SPEC 8.2, 10.4: createRepo carries the genesis state and its first commit, accepted together or not at all; a client publish of the genesis without the commit is a malformed request: bad_request, nothing stored.

scenarios.name: content-hosts-empty
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 rule 5: hosts is not empty; this state lists no host. The seq 2 state is validly signed and links to the tip, so the content rule decides: bad_request.

scenarios.name: content-owner-not-member
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 rule 5: members contains exactly one entry whose ed25519PublicKey equals ownerKey; this state lists only alice. The seq 2 state is validly signed and links to the tip, so the content rule decides: bad_request.

scenarios.name: content-member-epoch-mismatch
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 rule 5: every member's keyEpoch equals the state's keyEpoch; alice's entry says 1 in an epoch 0 state. The seq 2 state is validly signed and links to the tip, so the content rule decides: bad_request.

scenarios.name: content-home-host-not-listed
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 rule 5: every member's homeHostKey equals the hostKey of an entry in hosts; alice's home is c.vault.example, which is not listed. The seq 2 state is validly signed and links to the tip, so the content rule decides: bad_request.

scenarios.name: content-repo-id-changed
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 rule 5: repoId is unchanged from the previous state; this one names another repository. The seq 2 state is validly signed and links to the tip, so the content rule decides: bad_request.

scenarios.name: content-owner-key-changed
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 rule 5: ownerKey is unchanged from the previous state; this one, signed by alice, names alice as ownerKey. The seq 2 state is validly signed and links to the tip, so the content rule decides: bad_request.

scenarios.name: content-scheme-id-changed
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 rule 5: schemeId is unchanged from the previous state. The seq 2 state is validly signed and links to the tip, so the content rule decides: bad_request.

scenarios.name: content-genesis-nonce-after-seq-1
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 rule 5: genesisNonce is empty after seq 1 (also a rule 1 length); this seq 2 state repeats the 16-byte nonce. The seq 2 state is validly signed and links to the tip, so the content rule decides: bad_request.

scenarios.name: content-epoch-jump-2
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 rule 5: keyEpoch equals the previous keyEpoch or the previous keyEpoch + 1; this state jumps from 0 to 2. The seq 2 state is validly signed and links to the tip, so the content rule decides: bad_request.

scenarios.name: content-removed-key-still-member
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 rule 5: no member's ed25519PublicKey equals the memberKey of any removal; bob is removed and still listed. The seq 3 state is validly signed and links to the tip, so the content rule decides: bad_request.

scenarios.name: content-removed-at-seq-out-of-range
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 rule 5: every removal's removedAtSeq is at most the state's manifestSeq, and a new removal's equals it; bob's says 4 in a seq 3 state. The seq 3 state is validly signed and links to the tip, so the content rule decides: bad_request.

scenarios.name: content-new-removal-of-non-member
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 rule 5: every new removal names a key that was a member of the previous state; carol never was. The seq 3 state is validly signed and links to the tip, so the content rule decides: bad_request.

scenarios.name: content-owner-removed
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 rule 5: ownerKey is never removed (and members contains the owner exactly once); this state removes the owner. The seq 3 state is validly signed and links to the tip, so the content rule decides: bad_request.

scenarios.name: content-earlier-removal-altered
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 rule 5: every removal of the previous state appears unchanged (memberKey, removedAtSeq, and frontier); seq 4 repeats bob's removal with an empty frontier: bad_request.

scenarios.name: content-earlier-removal-omitted
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 rule 5: removals are cumulative, every removal of the previous state appears unchanged; seq 4 drops bob's removal: bad_request.

scenarios.name: genesis-epoch-not-zero
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 rule 3, 6.2: the genesis state MUST have keyEpoch 0; this one has 1: bad_request, nothing stored.

scenarios.name: genesis-extra-member
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 rule 3, 6.2: the genesis state MUST have exactly one member, the owner; this one also lists alice: bad_request, nothing stored.

scenarios.name: genesis-with-removals
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 rule 3, 6.2: the genesis state MUST have no removals; this one removes bob: bad_request, nothing stored.

scenarios.name: manifest-drops-this-host
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 rule 6, 8.6: a valid seq 2 state lists only b.vault.example (the owner's home moved to b); at a.vault.example it is not_hosted and the tip stays at genesis.

scenarios.name: manifest-malformed-structure
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 rule 1, 4.2: a seq 2 state with a host listed twice, a wrappedDataKey ciphertext of 47 bytes (not 48), a 63-byte ownerSignature, or a 31-byte prevManifestHash is malformed: bad_request each; the intact state is then accepted.

scenarios.name: commit-malformed-structure
scenarios.description: SPEC 7.1, 4.3: a commit listing the same parent twice, with an 11-byte iv, a 63-byte authorSignature, or a 15-byte ciphertext (shorter than the GCM tag) is malformed: bad_request each; the intact commit is then accepted.

scenarios.name: commit-with-held-parent-held
scenarios.description: SPEC 7.4, 6.5: as in diverged-owner-commit-held, rotL and a1 are held once W3 wins. alice's a3 cites the winning W3 correctly (member, epoch 0) but its parent a1 is held, so a3 is held too: forbidden.

scenarios.name: losing-rotation-commit-kept-held
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.5, 8.3: holding W3 (removes bob, epoch 1), the host is offered the losing L3 (removes carol, epoch 1, higher hash) with its rotation commit: L3 loses (manifest_conflict) and is retained, and its rotation commit is kept with it as a held commit.

scenarios.name: losing-commit-failing-cutoff-rejected
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.5 (1), 7.3: bob's b1 cites the retained losing L3 at epoch 1. The removal cutoff takes precedence: bob is removed in the tip W3 with frontier {root} and b1 is neither in it nor an ancestor of it, so b1 is rejected (forbidden), never held.

scenarios.name: held-commit-dropped-on-author-removal
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.5 drop test, 7.3: rotL and alice's a1 are held once W3 wins. W4 removes alice (epoch 1) with frontier {root}: a1 is not covered, so it is dropped. rotL meets no drop test and W4 lists the owner at its epoch 1, so it is accepted beside W4's rotation commit.

scenarios.name: chain-switch-drops-by-cutoff
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.5, 7.3: the host holds H3 (adds carol) and accepts bob's b1 citing it. W3 (removes bob, epoch 1, frontier {root}, lower hash) then wins with its rotation commit. Re-checking b1 against the winning chain, the removal cutoff takes precedence and b1 fails it: dropped; the rotation commit is the only head.

scenarios.name: held-descendants-accepted-in-turn
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.5: carol's c1 and its child c2 cite the losing L3 and are held when W3 wins. W4 re-invites carol at epoch 0: c1 is accepted, and its held descendant c2 is re-checked in turn and accepted, leaving c2 the only head.

scenarios.name: leave-dropped-on-removal
scenarios.description: SPEC 8.4: the host keeps bob's and alice's leave requests and drops bob's once a state removes bob; alice's stays pending.

scenarios.name: leave-latest-per-member
scenarios.description: SPEC 8.4: the host keeps the latest leave request per member; alice sends one and then a later one, and only the later one is pending.

scenarios.name: pending-losing-commit-rechecked-when-decided
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.5, 7.3, 7.4: the host holds H3 (adds carol, epoch 0) and accepts bob's b1 citing it. W3 (removes bob at epoch 1 with frontier {x}, lower hash) then wins; x, bob's child of b1, is unknown, so b1's cutoff is undecided and b1 MUST NOT stay accepted. When x arrives its header decides the cutoff (b1 is an ancestor of x), and b1, which cites a losing state, is re-checked by SPEC 6.5: W3 does not list bob, and the drop test holds (tip epoch 1 exceeds b1's 0), so b1 is dropped. x's parent is then rejected: forbidden. The rotation commit is the only head.

scenarios.name: stale-publish-with-content-violation
scenarios.description: SPEC 6.1 (the host answers with the first failure, in rule order), 6.3: while the tip is seq 2, a client publishes another seq 2 state on genesis that also lists no host. Rule 4 (chain link: a client state MUST be at tip + 1) fails before rule 5 (content), so the answer is manifest_conflict, not bad_request.

scenarios.name: pending-commit-resolved-by-losing-rotation-header
scenarios.description: SPEC 7.3, 6.5, 8.3: bob's b1 (citing seq 2) is accepted. W3 removes bob at epoch 1 with frontier {rotL}; rotL is unknown here, so b1's cutoff cannot be decided and b1 MUST NOT stay accepted. L3 (removes alice, epoch 1, higher hash) then arrives with its rotation commit rotL, whose parent is b1: L3 loses the tie rule (manifest_conflict) and rotL is kept held with it (SPEC 8.3). Ancestry for the cutoff follows every verified header whether or not accepted (SPEC 7.3), so b1 is an ancestor of frontier commit rotL; covered, and citing the winning seq 2 where bob is a member at epoch 0, b1 is accepted again.
